content:
maya: FYI — taking over primary for the 6pm->6am PST window. Leaving notes on access checks and coverage gaps. Please confirm before I drop off so we don't start a page with missing permissions.

aj: thanks — quick checklist?

maya: TL;DR: primary=maya, secondary=aj, escalation=ian. PagerDuty creds: everyone on rotation should have admin-lite (respond/ack/annotate) for our oncall schedule and escalation rules. AWS access: assume-role to prod-oncall role via SSO, with CloudWatch and EC2 Read/SSM Session Manager permissions. Grafana: viewer + alert acknowledge permission (team:eng-oncall). Runbook pointer: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/oncall-handoff (check the "Access & Escalation" section).

ian: noting a gap: liz still doesn't have the prod-oncall assume-role bound to her SSO group. She can be secondary if we grant it now but we should avoid last-minute role changes during a page.

liz: yep — I don't see the prod-oncall role in my AWS Console. Asked infra-iam earlier; no reply yet. If needed I can handle lower-impact jobs but can't assume full escalation.

ops-bot: [automated message] PagerDuty schedule snapshot: next shift start 2024-06-10T18:00:00Z. Current oncall: maya (primary), aj (secondary). Escalation policy: 5m -> aj, 10m -> ian.

maya: @liz — if infra-iam can't update role quickly, tell me and I'll reassign secondary to @ian for this shift. We want people with assume-role working.

aj: Access verification steps I'm about to run — please confirm results: 1) PagerDuty login + ability to acknowledge test alert; 2) AWS: run `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/prod-oncall --role-session-name oncall-check` and then `aws s3 ls` (should list prod-monitoring bucket); 3) Grafana: open alerts.redwood/grafana -> click an alert -> acknowledge.

maya: I'll run them and paste outputs (redacted).

maya: PagerDuty: logged in, can ack. UI shows my user in schedule.

maya: AWS assume-role OK, got temp creds. Ran `aws s3 ls s3://prod-monitoring` -> got bucket contents list.

maya: Grafana: clicked alert #INC-739, acknowledged successfully.

aj: great. @liz can you paste whatever errors you see from the IAM console or SSO portal?

liz: When I try to switch role via SSO I get: `You don't have permission to switch to this role (AccessDenied)`. The AWS console shows no inline policy attached for the prod-oncall role to my user.

ian: tagging infra-iam: @infra-iam-team — liz needs prod-oncall assume-role bound to eng-oncall group for tonight's rotation. Can we get a quick ACL patch? If not, we should make ian secondary instead.

incident-bot: [automated] Incident test alert sent to oncall. Please ack to verify routing.

maya: acked incident-bot test. Routing looks good.

aj: ian, if you can be secondary for this window please confirm.

ian: I can take secondary for tonight. I have assume-role access already.

maya: ok switching plan: primary=maya, secondary=ian, backup=aj, liz=observability support (no escalate). I'll update the PagerDuty override and post a short note in the rotation doc.

maya: PagerDuty override set: `pd override add --schedule oncall-main --start 2024-06-10T18:00:00Z --end 2024-06-11T06:00:00Z --user maya` (ops-bot confirmed).

ops-bot: [automated] PagerDuty override applied by maya for schedule oncall-main (start 2024-06-10T18:00:00Z).

aj: runbook pointers for responders if a page comes in: 1) Check PagerDuty alert -> annotations for service and runbook link. 2) If it's latency/customer-facing, go to Grafana dashboard: https://alerts.redwood/grafana/d/prod/latency-overview. 3) If backend error spikes, use CloudWatch logs + `aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id>` to debug. 4) For hot rollback, see deploy-runbook section: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/deploy-rollback.

maya: note on annotations: when acknowledging, add brief note with steps you're taking (e.g., "investigating grafana alert -> checking kv-cache hit rate"). This saves time for handoff.

liz: I'll ask infra-iam for role fix and cc infra-pagers. If they can't move fast, I'll shadow and be available for non-escalation tasks (alerts triage/Slack comms).

ian: when you get access, do the assume-role check from aj's steps and post screenshot/command output. That verifies we can escalate to you mid-incident.

maya: final checklist before I leave: - confirm PD override applied (done) - confirm Grafana & AWS assume-role works for primary (done) - confirm secondary has assume-role or we have override set (ian confirmed) - document coverage gap (liz) and contact infra-iam.

aj: quick note about credentials auditing: if someone new joins rotation, ops-iam will do a 24h grace period where they can be oncall but with limited escalation. Make sure to record any exceptions in the rotation doc.

ops-bot: [automated] Handoff summary posted to /archives/oncall-handoffs: 2024-06-10 maya -> END SHIFT 6pm->6am (primary: maya, secondary: ian, backup: aj).

maya: thanks — I'll sign off at 17:55. Ping me if infra-iam responds.

liz: thanks all, filing infra request now.

ian: good handoff. GL and see you in the morning.

maya: closing thread — any followups, please start a new thread tagged #oncall-handoff with the timestamp.
